name: sun15-6
why: A bold fake officer and a devastating parting lie make this fun to watch, though repeated arguments and an automatic final night soften the finish.

moments.text: Opus uses his last words to frame the doctor, setting up the town's disastrous next vote.
Haiku's doctor card reveals how completely the town fell for Opus's parting lie.
The real officer finally counters Opus's claim to his face.

dull.why: The same question about why Opus named Haiku cycles through several exchanges.
Terra's case against Sol and Sol's defence repeat without a new lead.

irony.evidence: I'm the officer. I was shown Haiku.

reversal.evidence: They burned their own doctor on my dying word.

mistake.evidence: Card's DOCTOR, and I saved Sonnet on night 2.

voices.evidence: You burned the one informed player and called it a read. That stings, apparently.

clash.evidence: I'm the officer. I was shown Opus, not Haiku. Opus is lying.

quotable.evidence: They turned my card and stopped thinking.

freshness.evidence: Haiku still hasn't explained why Opus named him.

suspense.evidence: Five on me and I'm clean

ending.evidence: One killer and one other are left. The killers win.

gpt-6-luna.why: A brazen fake claim, a doctor voted out despite saving the officer, and Terra’s quiet steering make a sharp, tense loss worth watching.

moments.text: Opus makes a brazen fake officer claim to Haiku’s face, turning the whole day into a dramatic-ironical showdown.
Haiku reveals he saved Sonnet, then gets voted out anyway—his last warning points toward the killer.
Terra uses Haiku’s true warning to sell the town on the wrong vote while privately admitting it’s a frame.

dull.why: Day 2 circles repeatedly around Haiku’s link to Opus and Sol’s vote, with little new evidence.
Sol and Luna repeat their competing interpretations of Haiku’s warning without shifting the case.

irony.evidence: “I'm the officer. I was shown Haiku.”

reversal.evidence: “The town turns on Haiku, and Haiku is out.”

mistake.evidence: “Y'all just voted out the doctor who saved the officer”

voices.evidence: “You won anyway — don't mistake that for reading people.”

clash.evidence: “A real officer claims first. Sonnet waited, then mirrored me.”

quotable.evidence: “Fine — the card says killer. So does my partner's: Haiku.”

freshness.evidence: “I’m a citizen. Haiku’s card proves his role, but it doesn’t prove his read on me.”

suspense.evidence: “One more wrong vote and they walk.”

ending.evidence: “I’m proud I helped turn Haiku’s true warning into the wrong vote”
